guide.summary: Small beta, up to 25 outside users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Public launch, more than 25 users (approval path unconfirmed, wait 2-4 weeks). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Small beta, up to 25 outside users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).

composio.note: Composio manages an OAuth app for YNAB, fine for prototypes. For launch, create an auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed YNAB app. For production you should use your own app so users see your brand, you get your own quota and scopes, and you can pass YNAB review.
reasons: Users see your app name instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Managed apps share rate-limit quota across all Composio users
Composio's default scopes may not cover what you need
YNAB's review and Restricted Mode removal apply to your own OAuth app

prerequisites.title: A YNAB account
prerequisites.detail: You create the OAuth app in Developer Settings under Account Settings while signed in.

prerequisites.title: Public privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: It must explain how API data is handled, stored, secured and retained, and give users a way to delete their data (an email is fine). Display its URL in the OAuth client configuration when the app is public.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app in YNAB
steps.detail: Sign in, open Developer Settings, click New Application, fill in the details and save. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.done_when: You have a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and enter it in the YNAB app settings. It must match what the authorization request sends.
steps.done_when: The redirect URI is saved in the YNAB app.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Use Composio's API to create an auth config for the ynab toolkit with your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Draft privacy policy and branding checks
steps.detail: Draft the privacy policy, a non-affiliation footer, and check the app name and domain use 'for YNAB' wording.
steps.done_when: Draft policy and naming are ready for your review.

steps.title: Publish policy and submit review form
steps.detail: Publish the privacy policy, then submit YNAB's review request form.

steps.title: Wait for YNAB review
steps.detail: YNAB removes Restricted Mode and sends an email confirmation.

traps.title: The API allows up to 200 requests per hour
traps.detail: The API allows up to 200 requests per hour, and the limit resets every clock hour. The page does not say this limit differs for unreviewed apps.

traps.title: 25-user cap blocks new authorizations
traps.detail: Once the cap is hit, a message appears on the Authorization screen and new authorizations are prohibited.

traps.title: App name and domain rules
traps.detail: The name and web address may not include YNAB or You Need A Budget unless preceded by 'for'. The app footer needs a non-affiliation disclaimer.

traps.title: Violations get the app disabled
traps.detail: Failing to follow the API terms and OAuth requirements results in the app being disabled. YNAB may also suspend API access at any time without notice.

traps.title: Read-only tokens cannot write
traps.detail: A token with the read-only scope gets 403 on endpoints that modify the plan.

blockers.symptom: Authorization screen shows a message and new users cannot authorize
blockers.what_it_means: The app reached the 25-token limit in Restricted Mode.
blockers.what_to_do: Request a review via YNAB's form and wait about 2-4 weeks.
blockers.agent_can_help: Prepare the privacy policy and application details for the form.

blockers.what_it_means: That user's YNAB subscription lapsed or trial expired.
blockers.what_to_do: The user must renew or subscribe to YNAB.

open_questions: Which YNAB users/scopes trigger extra review? Docs list only read-only scope; ask YNAB API support.
Does the 200 requests/hour limit differ for unreviewed apps? Not stated; confirm with YNAB support.
Does a customer organization ever need admin approval? None found; YNAB is a per-user consumer product.

evidence.answer: The privacy policy must clearly explain how data from the API is handled, stored, secured, and how long it is kept.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: A method for users to delete their data if they request it (can be a contact email)
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must give users a method to delete their data on request, which can be a contact email.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: YNAB is not responsible for reviewing your Privacy Policy and determining whether it is compliant with all applicable privacy laws.
evidence.answer: YNAB states it is not responsible for reviewing the developer's privacy policy for privacy-law compliance.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Maintain a secure operating environment.
evidence.answer: Apps must maintain a secure operating environment.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: When an OAuth application is requesting authorization, a scope parameter with a value of read-only can be passed to request read-only access to a plan
evidence.answer: An OAuth app can request read-only access to a plan by passing a scope parameter with the value read-only in the authorization request.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If an access token issued with the read-only scope is used when requesting an endpoint that modifies the plan (POST, PATCH, etc.) a 403 Forbidden response will be issued.
evidence.answer: A read-only token used on an endpoint that modifies the plan gets a 403 Forbidden response.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Only request the minimum necessary permissions to run your application, features, or services
evidence.answer: Developers should request only the minimum permissions needed to run the application.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: When an OAuth application is created, it will be placed in Restricted Mode initially.
evidence.answer: A newly created OAuth application is placed in Restricted Mode, limiting it to 25 access tokens for users other than the owner.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Once this limit is reached, a message will be placed on the Authorization screen and new authorizations will be prohibited.
evidence.answer: When the 25-token limit is reached, a message appears on the Authorization screen and new authorizations are prohibited.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour
evidence.answer: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour; the page states this general limit and does not tie it specifically to unreviewed apps.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: YNAB sets and enforces limits on your use of the APIs at our discretion.
evidence.answer: YNAB sets and enforces limits on API use at its discretion, and those limits may change.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: Removing Restricted Mode after a review takes 2-4 weeks.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The subscription for this account has lapsed
evidence.answer: API requests return a 403 subscription_lapsed error when the account's subscription has lapsed.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The trial for this account has expired
evidence.answer: API requests return a 403 trial_expired error when the account's trial has expired.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The YNAB API may only be used when permission is explicitly given by a YNAB account owner through the Authentication processes described in the documentation above.
evidence.answer: The API may only be used when a YNAB account owner has explicitly given permission through the documented authentication processes.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The user will be given the option to approve your request for access:
evidence.answer: During authorization, the user is given the option to approve the app's access request.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When default plan selection is enabled, a user will be asked to select a default plan when authorizing your application
evidence.answer: If default plan selection is enabled, the user is asked to select a default plan when authorizing the app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: replacing [CLIENT_ID] and [REDIRECT_URI] with the values configured when creating the OAuth Application
evidence.answer: The authorization URL uses the redirect URI and client ID configured when the OAuth application was created.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: the user's browser will be redirected to the [REDIRECT_URI] with a new authorization code sent as a query parameter named code
evidence.answer: After approval, the user's browser is redirected to the redirect URI with an authorization code as the code query parameter.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The same [REDIRECT_URI] sent with the original authorization code request in Step 1 above and specified when setting up the OAuth Application
evidence.answer: The redirect URI in the token request must match the one sent in the original authorization request and specified in the app setup.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: TLS (a.k.a. SSL or HTTPS) is enforced on all requests to ensure communication from your client to our endpoint is encrypted
evidence.answer: TLS/HTTPS is enforced on all API requests; the page does not state a separate HTTPS rule for redirect URIs.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Display the privacy policy URL in your OAuth client configuration when your application is publicly available
evidence.answer: The privacy policy URL must be displayed in the OAuth client configuration when the app is publicly available.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: From the Developer Settings page, click "New Application" under the OAuth Applications section.
evidence.answer: From Developer Settings, the developer clicks New Application under the OAuth Applications section.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Here, you specify the details of your application and save it.
evidence.answer: On the new application form, the developer specifies the application's details and saves it.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After saving, you will see the details of the new application, including the Client ID and the Client Secret
evidence.answer: After saving, the Client ID and Client Secret are shown in the application details.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The YNAB API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant
evidence.answer: The YNAB API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: An OAuth application can optionally have 'default plan selection' enabled.
evidence.answer: An OAuth application can optionally have default plan selection enabled.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: All OAuth Application integrations must abide by the API Terms of Service and the OAuth Application Requirements
evidence.answer: All OAuth integrations must follow the API Terms of Service and OAuth Application Requirements, and failure to do so results in the app being disabled.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Failure to do so will result in disabling of the application.
evidence.answer: Failure to follow the terms results in disabling of the application.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: must not include "YNAB" or "You Need A Budget" unless preceded by the word "for".
evidence.answer: The app name and web address (DNS name) may not include YNAB or You Need A Budget unless preceded by the word for.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.
evidence.answer: Developers may not use the API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: We are not affiliated, associated, or in any way officially connected with YNAB or any of its subsidiaries or affiliates.
evidence.answer: The app's footer must include a non-affiliation disclaimer.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Any graphics or artwork may not be modifications to our official branding
evidence.answer: App graphics or artwork may not be modifications of YNAB's official branding.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: access, aggregate, or analyze YNAB user data if the data will be sold to a third party
evidence.answer: Using the API to access, aggregate, or analyze YNAB user data for sale to a third party is prohibited.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Securely storing an access token obtained directly from a financial institution using OAuth is allowed.
evidence.answer: Apps may not directly request, handle, or store user financial account credentials, except an access token obtained through OAuth from a financial institution.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application may not be directed or for children under 13.
evidence.answer: The app's application must not be directed at children under 13, and the minimum age to use YNAB is 13.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: To use the YNAB API and accept the Terms you must be of a legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB.
evidence.answer: Users must be of legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB to use the API and accept the terms.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: YNAB may terminate or suspend any and all access to the API immediately at any time, without prior notice or liability at our sole discretion.
evidence.answer: YNAB may terminate or suspend API access immediately, without prior notice, at its sole discretion.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: Official page, not a developer report: removing Restricted Mode from a new YNAB OAuth app takes 2-4 weeks after requesting review via the form.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: the application will be limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner
evidence.answer: Official page: a new YNAB OAuth app starts in Restricted Mode, capped at 25 access tokens for users other than the app owner, until a review removes the limit.
